analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. README.md adds an index link to the new add-on IPC reference. In cli-reference.md, head line 1758 adds the add-on runtime path row; the other changed ranges (156, 904-932) fall in excerpts not supplied in this batch. The replayed lines 1302-2005 are otherwise unchanged context covering cache location, benchmarks, logs, report, and env passthrough, and none of those regress T-041 or the cache controls.

addon-hold-ipc.md is the new attack surface. It documents a same-user AF_UNIX socket with these properties:
- 8 KiB line limit, at most 8 connections, 300 s idle timeout.
- Per-request peer verification: LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit token, then a SecCode requirement anchored to team SLDQ2GJ6TL and identifier io.darkbloom.sandbox with hardened runtime.
- A DEBUG-only dev identity.
- Holds can drain or pause serving, and a lease persists while ownership.lock is held.

The doc cites TB-012, which the base model lacks; this is reported as a threat-model gap. Because the provider and add-on share a user, ADV-001 already controls the host, so this surface adds no confidentiality loss to A-001 or A-003.

Open questions, unverifiable without source (AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonPeerPolicy.swift, AddonCommand.swift):
- Is DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET honored in release builds?
- Does the DEBUG identity truly compile out?
- How do holds feed the busy fields sent to the coordinator, and do they affect routing or billing?
- Does the `darkbloom addon` mailbox command bind to live process identity as claimed?

findings.detail: docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md documents a new local AF_UNIX `hold.v1` control surface (~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock). Over it, a code-signed add-on can make the provider drain or hold serving capacity, and an expired lease is kept while the add-on holds ownership.lock. The doc points readers to threat-model `TB-012` (line 96), but the base canonical model defines boundaries only through TB-011. No asset, threat or mitigation covers this boundary. Nothing in the model covers the same-user peer-token and code-requirement check, the DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY` acceptance, the `DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET` path override, or the indefinite availability hold through ownership.lock. The new `darkbloom addon` lifecycle-mailbox commands in cli-reference.md are also unmodeled. Trigger: a reviewer relies on TB-012 to evaluate this surface, but no TB-012 exists. Impact: provider availability and drain controls stay unreviewed against TB-003 and TB-002. The model also does not record that busy fields reported to the coordinator are self-reported. Fix: add TB-012 and its threats to docs/threat-model.yaml. The new entries should record that the socket is not a boundary against the same user. They should state whether release builds honor DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET. They should also bound how long a hold can persist.
findings.title: New add-on hold IPC surface cites an undefined threat-model boundary (TB-012)
